clue.text: Small matter of creating plaster cast

definitions.note: a tiny bit of matter studied in physics

indicators.note: to cast something is to throw or mould it into a new shape, so these letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: A sculptor makes a small item by moulding a plaster cast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' looks like part of the plaster scene, but it tells you to rearrange the letters of CREATING PLASTER. 'of' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A strange particle is a subatomic particle in physics, so it is a very small piece of matter.

clue.text: Perhaps incurable mental disorder won't be contracted

explanation.surface: A psychiatric condition so stubborn that no-one will catch it.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whimsically, a condition is resistant to the shrink (slang for a psychiatrist), so it may be incurable. Read literally, fabric that resists shrinking will not contract in the wash.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrink-resistant cloth will not contract when washed; jokingly, a disorder that resists the psychiatrist is perhaps incurable.

clue.text: Broke the ice when on them

definitions.text: Broke the ice when on them

parts.words: Broke the ice when on them
parts.note: a drink served on these is poured over ice, and to be on these is also to be broke, with no money

explanation.surface: Someone started a conversation while standing on something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broke' looks like a verb with 'the ice'; it is the adjective meaning penniless, and 'on the rocks' means both bankrupt and served with ice.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'on the rocks' means both penniless and of a drink poured over ice cubes.

clue.text: Heard nothing is hard as a sister

indicators.note: what is heard is spoken, so the words before are said aloud and spelt another way

parts.note: nothing means none, followed by is
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Someone who heard nothing finds it as hard as being a nun.
explanation.walkthrough: NONE IS said aloud sounds like NUNNIS; add H for hard.
explanation.definitionFit: Nunnish is an adjective for behaving like a nun, a religious sister.

clue.text: Run to seed: save cutting

indicators.note: something put to seed is planted inside, so one piece goes into another

parts.note: save in the sense of but or apart from, as in all save one
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A gardener plans to let a plant run to seed and save cuttings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'save' is not about keeping anything: it means 'except'. 'to seed' plants R inside EXCEPT.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutting from a newspaper or book is an extract, a passage taken out of the whole.

clue.text: What's not paid for a car, we hear

parts.note: RR stands for Rolls-Royce, the luxury car
the organs we hear with are the ears

explanation.surface: Someone says payments on their car have not been made.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' looks like a sound-alike signal but stands for EARS, what we hear with. 'for' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrears are payments that are due but still unpaid, money owed and overdue.

clue.text: Propose a top class scene

parts.note: to table a motion is to propose it for discussion
U is a British term for upper class, socially acceptable

explanation.surface: Someone suggests a first-rate setting for a play.
explanation.walkthrough: U for upper class is a British usage popularised in the 1950s.
explanation.definitionFit: A tableau is a picture-like scene, often posed by actors who stay still.

clue.text: King heartlessly hogs best part of drug in land of pleasure

indicators.note: the letters AI form a part of the word for the drug, and that part is swapped for the larger piece

parts.note: cocaine is the drug

indicators.note: to hog something is to hold on to it, so one piece holds another
without a heart means the middle letters of the word are removed

parts.note: a monarch, the word itself here
AI, read as A1, means first class or the best

explanation.surface: A heartless monarch keeps the best of the drugs for himself in a pleasure paradise.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 means first-rate, so 'best' is written AI. 'heartlessly' drops the middle of the monarch's word, and 'part of' marks the two letters inside the drug's name that get replaced. 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Cockaigne is the imaginary medieval land of luxury and idleness, a mythical paradise of pleasure.

clue.text: Once sober geezer who reformed?

indicators.note: something reformed is formed again into a new shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A bloke who once drank too much and changed his ways.
explanation.walkthrough: Dickens's miser, who changes his ways at the end of A Christmas Carol, is spelt out by rearranging ONCE SOBER GEEZER. 'Geezer' is British slang for a man.
explanation.definitionFit: Ebenezer Scrooge, the miser in A Christmas Carol, reforms after visits from ghosts.

clue.text: It has a formula for power

definitions.text: It has a formula for power

parts.words: It has a formula for power
parts.note: reads like a scientific equation, but Formula One is a category of motor sport with powerful vehicles

explanation.surface: Something holding a mathematical formula for power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'formula' suggests science; it is a class of motor racing, such as Formula One.
explanation.definitionFit: A car built for racing is entered in a formula, a class of motor sport defined by rules.

clue.text: German first battling on the firing line?

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the next word is taken

parts.note: the oche is the line darts players throw from

explanation.surface: A German soldier fights first on the front line.
explanation.walkthrough: The OCHE is the line behind which a player stands in darts, a pub game popular in Britain. 'on' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Boche is a derogatory old slang term for a German, especially a soldier.

clue.text: Point when row gets worse

parts.note: N for north, a point of the compass
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
a tier is a row, as of seats

explanation.surface: An argument gets worse at a certain moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' looks like an argument, but here it is a line of seats. 'gets' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Nastier is a comparative meaning more unpleasant, so it can stand for worse.

clue.text: Lost head to be angry and mean

indicators.note: losing its head means the word drops its first letter

parts.note: to rave is to talk wildly in anger
to rage is to be furious

explanation.surface: Someone loses their head and gets angry and nasty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'be angry' gives two pieces: RAVE, which drops its first letter to become AVE, then RAGE. 'mean' looks like nasty; here it means average.
explanation.definitionFit: The mean of a set of numbers is its average, a statistical synonym.

clue.text: Compound clockwise for a male horse character

parts.note: per means for each, as in miles per hour
a man is a male
eta is a letter of the Greek alphabet
a nag is an old horse

explanation.surface: A clockwise compound for a man who rides horses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clockwise' explains the grid: going round the four lights clockwise, 24 runs right to left and 16 runs upwards, so the last two pieces appear backwards and the whole reads PERMANGANATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Permanganate is a chemical compound, a salt of permanganic acid, such as potassium permanganate.

clue.text: Chatterboxes check on the wheel

indicators.note: to box something is to fight it or knock it about, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Gossips keep an eye on someone at the steering wheel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chatterboxes' must be split into CHATTER and 'boxes', which tells you to rearrange CHATTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A ratchet is a toothed wheel with a catch that stops it turning backwards, a check on its motion.

clue.text: Expert on infusion from dummy flower

parts.note: a teat is a baby's rubber dummy or bottle nipple
an aster is a daisy-like flower

explanation.surface: Someone skilled with herbal infusions made from a flower.
explanation.walkthrough: A dummy is the British word for a baby's pacifier. 'from' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea taster is a professional who judges tea, an infusion of leaves in hot water.

clue.text: See 13
Cross about hearing 24 after second run

indicators.note: one piece is placed after the other
about means around, so one piece goes round another

parts.note: a mule is a cross between a horse and a donkey

indicators.note: what is heard is said aloud, so the word is spelt by its sound

parts.note: the answer to 24 is an old horse, and a horse is a gee-gee in nursery talk

explanation.surface: Someone is annoyed at hearing about the next item after a second race.
explanation.walkthrough: Gee-gee is a child's word for a horse, and it sounds like two letters. 'Cross' looks like angry; here it is a hybrid animal, the offspring of a horse and a donkey.
explanation.definitionFit: To run goods is to smuggle them, bringing contraband in secretly.

clue.text: See 13
Spree end here in Berlin

parts.note: the Spree is the river through Berlin, and it ends where it joins the Havel in a western district of the city

explanation.surface: A spending spree ends here in the German capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spree' looks like a shopping binge; it is the river Spree, which flows into the Havel in western Berlin.
explanation.definitionFit: Spandau, a borough of Berlin, is where the river Spree meets the Havel.

clue.text: Put out order: "En garde!"

indicators.note: putting things in order rearranges them, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A fencing master calls for order with an 'En garde!'
explanation.walkthrough: 'order' tells you to rearrange EN GARDE.
explanation.definitionFit: To derange is to disturb or upset, putting someone out of their normal state.

clue.text: Free single turned up, say

parts.note: unmarried, not wed

indicators.note: in a down light, turning up means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: EG, for example, means say

explanation.surface: A single person turns up free, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' suits a down light: the abbreviation for 'say' is read from the bottom up.
explanation.definitionFit: To unwedge something is to free it, loosening it from where it is stuck.

clue.text: Light fillers

parts.note: in crosswords a light is a grid entry, so this means what fills the lights

explanation.surface: Something that fills in a lamp or a light meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Light' looks like a lamp or a light meal; in crossword language a light is a space in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Solutions are written into a crossword's lights, so they are what fills them.

clue.text: Silver rings solidify on evergreen

indicators.note: rings means goes round, so one piece encircles another

parts.note: AG is the chemical symbol for silver
to gel is to set solid
taken as written

explanation.surface: Silver rings set firmly on a fir tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'evergreen' looks like a tree but is used in its sense of lasting forever; 'Silver' is split open to hold the two other pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Evergreen in its figurative sense means everlasting, lasting for ages.

clue.text: For example, wrack by fear in issue

indicators.note: one piece placed inside another

parts.note: seed means issue or offspring, as in biblical language
awe is reverent fear

explanation.surface: Someone is wracked by fear about their children.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrack' looks like the verb rack; it is a brown seaweed found on rocky shores. 'by' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Wrack is a kind of brown marine alga, so it is one example of seaweed.

clue.text: See 13
Overturned covers trapping gold bird

indicators.note: turned over means the whole word is read backwards
to trap something is to hold it inside

parts.note: wraps are coverings
OR is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: Upturned covers trap a gold-coloured bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overturned' turns the whole assembly round, not just the covers; heraldry's word for gold is a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: The sparrow is a small brown songbird.

clue.text: A rum one oozing charm

indicators.note: something oozing leaks and loses its shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A glass of rum giving off charm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oozing' looks as if it goes with 'charm', but it tells you to rearrange A RUM ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: To enamour is to charm or captivate someone, filling them with love.

clue.text: Once used in jest about tips for spirited communicator

indicators.note: the tip of each word is its opening letter, taken in turn

explanation.surface: A board once used as a joke for talking to ghosts.
explanation.walkthrough: The first letters of ONCE USED IN JEST ABOUT spell the answer. 'spirited' is a pun on spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: A Ouija board is used at seances to talk with spirits, so it communicates with the dead.

clue.text: Jacket's not about to be withdrawn in London

indicators.note: drawn back means the letters are read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
CA, short for circa, means about

explanation.surface: A jacket is not going to be taken out of service in London.
explanation.walkthrough: NOT and CA read backwards give the answer; 'in London' adds that ACTON is also a district of west London. An acton was a padded jacket worn under armour.
explanation.definitionFit: An acton is a quilted jacket worn under medieval armour.

clue.text: Two hundred and one in protest bound by the dozen

parts.note: a duo is a pair

indicators.note: one piece placed inside another

parts.note: a demo is a protest march
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Two hundred and one people at a protest held together in twelves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bound' means bound as a book: a duodecimo is a book size made by folding each sheet into twelve leaves. 'and' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Duodecimo is a book size made from sheets folded into twelve leaves, a format bound in twelves.

clue.text: Man's form of charge to people's fun event

parts.note: the heraldic emblem of the Isle of Man shows three legs joined at the hip
a race is a people or ethnic group

explanation.surface: A man charges people for a fun event.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Man is a British crown dependency whose emblem is three running legs; a charge is a heraldic design. 'to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A three-legged race is a fun event at a sports day, where pairs run with two legs tied together.
